did.abstract: 32 black and white photographs of Italian immigrants engaged in various activities at Gregg Chapel, the Italian branch of Lafayette Avenue Presbyterian Church at 190 4th Avenue, Brooklyn.

altformavail.head: Existence and Location of Copies
altformavail.p: The digitized portions of this collection are available on our digital collections under the call number prefix GREGG.

arrangement.head: Arrangement
arrangement.p: This small collection is housed in a single folder with no particular arrangement.

bioghist.head: Historical note
bioghist.p: Gregg Chapel opened circa 1907-1908 at 190 4th Avenue in Brooklyn to serve the Italian immigrant population of the Gowanus area. It was a branch of the Lafayette Avenue Presbyterian Church and was intended to help Italian immigrants learn English and professional skills as well as American customs such as basketball and the Pledge of Allegiance. In 1913, the building was renovated and improved. The chapel held its final services in the building in 1948.

processinfo.p: The photographs were digitized and described on the item level at some point following their acquisition in 2008. The collection was rehoused and this finding created by Dee Bowers in 2026.

scopecontent.head: Scope and Contents
scopecontent.p: 32 black and white photographs of Italian immigrants engaged in various activities at Gregg Chapel, the Italian branch of Lafayette Avenue Presbyterian Church at 190 4th Avenue, Brooklyn. Activities include English classes, millinery class, and sports such as basketball. Most of the prints are 8x10", though some are smaller. Named photographers include Al Vaccaro Photos, 159 W 9th St, Brooklyn; M.S. Gorodess, Brooklyn; and Chas. C. Zinsser, 419 E 82 St, NYC.
